title: India's Battery Storage Boom Is Outrunning Both Its Tariffs and Its Factories

version_history.note: New post: India's BESS/grid-storage market — installed capacity growth (1,082 MWh end-2025 to ~9.3 GWh mid-2026), the two VGF tranches, and the piece's central finding that discovered BESS tariffs fell roughly twice as fast (71-86%) as battery pack costs (36.5%) since 2022, per IEEFA/JMK Research, alongside the ACC PLI manufacturing scheme's 2.8%-of-target commissioning shortfall. Explicitly narrates three unreconciled data discrepancies (tendered-capacity units, PSP pipeline stage-counts, tariff-decline percentages) as a market-immaturity finding rather than resolving them. Every PIB/MNRE/CEA/IESA-attributed figure flagged as primary-by-attribution, secondary-by-access since pib.gov.in, mnre.gov.in, cea.nic.in and indiaesa.info were all blocked to direct fetch in this session. Includes one SVG chart (BESS tariff decline vs. battery-pack-cost benchmark) and two comparison tables. Published directly per explicit user instruction.
